title: Equivalence [A/𝒦] ≃ [B(Σ)/G] (RES theorem)
body_html:
Equivalence $[A / \mathscr{K}] \;\xrightarrow{\sim}\; [\BSigma / G]$

Define the category $[A / \mathscr{K}]$ on facets in $A$ with $$\Hom_{[A / \mathscr{K}]}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{E}) := \{kn \;|\; k \in K_\mathcal{E},\ n \in N,\ \mathcal{E} \subseteq \overline{n \mathcal{F}}\} \subseteq G,$$ and similarly $[\BSigma / G]$ on facets of $\BSigma$.

Lemma. $\Hom_{[A / \mathscr{K}]}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{E}) = \Hom_{[\BSigma / G]}(\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{E})$ for facets in $A$.

Theorem. The natural functor $\mathrm{RES} : [A / \mathscr{K}] \to [\BSigma / G]$ is an equivalence of categories.
proof_html:
Every facet of $\BSigma$ is $G$-conjugate to a facet in $A$ (so $\mathrm{RES}$ is essentially surjective); the lemma above gives fully-faithfulness. $\square$

The advantage: hypotheses about $\BSigma$ can be checked on the apartment $A$. The further refinement [𝒜/𝒦] ≃ [A/𝒦] (alcove reduction under (F5)–(F6)) reduces the apartment itself to a fundamental alcove.
